summary: A quest log you can pin to the map, redesigned map controls, a tidier Desk with a session chip, Review Inbox and party inventory, search everywhere, and an Android Back button that behaves.
features: Quest log: DMs write quests with a giver, a place, objectives, a promised reward and private DM notes, then reveal them to the whole party or to chosen characters. Mark objectives done or failed, add chronicle entries stamped with the session and campaign day, and close quests as completed or failed. Rewards are words plus links to receipts you already paid; writing or closing a quest never moves coins or items.

Players follow quests in Home → Quest log: Active, Done and Failed, a Follow pin, private notes and a Quest updated notice, with a New quest notice when the DM shares one while the app is open. Hidden objectives, DM notes and DM-only chronicle lines never reach players' devices. View as player shows the DM exactly what a chosen character sees, and quests also appear on the Desk, on NPC cards and in the map's Here sheet.

Quests on the map: tie a quest or any objective to a place, a map pin or a circle drawn over the map ("Harkon's horse is somewhere in here"). The map's Quests tool lists that map's quests and zooms to one, and Show on map in the quest log opens it there. Players only see the pins and areas the DM shared.

Map controls redesigned: on computers and tablets the tools stand in a rail on the right (Move, Play, Table and View, with Here and Plan journey beside everything else), a Layers panel chooses what shows on the map, zoom is a small pill in the corner, and ← Back opens the parent map while X Close map returns you to the screen you came from. Phones keep the bottom bar, and the map title, buttons and zoom follow your theme.

DMs place the party, markers, entrances, records, location links, fog, walls, lights, the combat token and the grid from a setup rail on the left, each with its own small panel beside the map; Ctrl+Z undoes fog. All map settings is grouped (This map, Places & party, Players & display, Exploration, Combat, View, Shortcuts & help) with a search box. An Initiative panel (press I) shows the round, turn order and hit points on the map; players see only the combatants revealed to them and their own character.

Search everything: a search button in the app header (or Ctrl+K / ⌘K) finds any screen, character, NPC, shop, place, map or item and opens common jobs like Add loot or New quest. Press ? for the shortcut list; players only find what their own screens already show.

Imported character-sheet equipment takes its value from the SRD (via Open5e) instead of arriving at zero, matched offline and preferring the sheet's edition; the import review lists every value found and every item without a match, and Fill missing values from the SRD prices items imported earlier.
Duplicate a shop with its stock, an encounter with its loot (reset to round 1), or an NPC's setup in one step; the original is untouched.

Undo a DM's shop purchase straight from its confirmation while the message is on screen: coins, stock and items come back exactly once, and it refuses if the items have since moved. Purchases, sales, transfers, Add loot and encounter awards now confirm with a View receipt button.

Session chip for DMs: the header shows "Session 12 · day 42" and opens End & start next, Session Time and what happened since the last session (loot awarded, money in and out, requests waiting, characters away). Pin to Desk adds any feature screen to a Pinned row on the Desk, and during a fight the Desk's party cards have −1 / +1 hit-point buttons.
improvements: Android: the Back button closes an open picker, menu, sheet or dialog first, then a map panel, and only then goes to the previous screen; on the first screen with a campaign open it asks you to press back again to exit. Status-bar icons turn dark on the light themes.

Phones turned sideways give most of the screen to the page: the section tabs become an icon rail on the left and the header hides while you scroll down. The title screen offers Continue · <campaign> · Session N for the campaign you last opened, and the Campaigns dialog lists the others by when you last opened them.

A tidier Desk: Session, Party, Funds, Market, Activity and Rolls as a 3×2 grid on a computer and a swipe strip with dots on a phone, End & start next at the top of the Session tile, a setup checklist for new campaigns, and empty readouts that point to a next step.

Main screens share one header with the title and main action in the same place, and the scene picture above each screen shrinks to a short band after your first visit (always short in split view and phone landscape).
Bigger tap targets: 24 px checkboxes with a full-width row to tap, each character's field permissions in a Permissions… sheet on the Party card, and larger close buttons and small links.

Review Inbox is one queue, oldest first, with who asked, what it does, the amount and the balance afterwards on every request; Approve is the gold button, Deny can take a remembered reason, decided requests stay in place as a short note, and Approve all payments under an amount approves each one once after a confirmation. Keyboard: A approves, D denies, J and K move.

Faster loot awards: finished encounters show on the Desk as Ready for loot review, each item is one short row with its value in gold, you can tick several items to assign or pool them at once, and a bottom bar keeps the total and Transfer loot in view. Loot is still transferred only once.

Party inventory lists each item once with an action menu (Edit, Give, Move to pool, Sell to shop, Remove), grouping, filters and search; select several items to give, pool or remove them, and Resume finishes a run interrupted by a reload without repeating anything. Players see their coins and Give under Combined wealth, identical items as one row, and the party screen is named Party & inventory.

Market opens with the shops you can visit; a shop's counter keeps a Paying from bar in view, remembers who last paid there, and DMs can pick Sell to a character once and sell each item with one tap. Shop editing has visible labels and one Save changes bar.

Encounter tracker on phones: a bottom bar keeps Prev, the round, whose turn it is and Next turn in reach, and each combatant shows its side (◆ ally, ✕ enemy). Session Time offers +1 h, +4 h, Long rest · 8 h and Next morning.
Copper fields show their gold value as you type and accept coins such as 2 gp 5 sp; gold amounts of 1,000 or more read with separators. Copper stays the saved amount.

Confirmations such as Discard changes? or Delete this? open in Lootsplitter's own style instead of a plain browser box, work the same on phones and in the Android app, and Escape or Back cancels. Delete current campaign lives in a Danger zone fold. Fields that save when you leave them show a Saved tick.

Joining a room is quicker: a join link finds the room's characters at once, the join card asks only for your character and your name, and you land on Home with a Getting started strip. Players see the DM's campaign name in the header, on the Campaign screen and in My account instead of Party overview.

Review Inbox's type filter and the inventory's Holder, Category and Equipped filters are remembered per campaign on this device; sections that open and close on Downtime, Party, Market and shop pages share one look, and the exchange board remembers whether you left it open.

Clearer names: the DM's home screen is the Desk everywhere, Shop Management is Shop schedules, and Downtime is Time & downtime. Old links still open the same screens. Help has a Guide for: Players | Dungeon Masters switch.

My account shows one section at a time (Campaigns, Characters, Profile, Backups, Support), with Resume leading each saved campaign; accounts that only play no longer see DM hosting details, and sign-in errors appear right under the form.

Accessibility: the first Tab on any screen offers Skip to content, Add loot and shop edit label every field, sheet tabs announce as tabs, gain and loss colours meet contrast in every theme, and the chat history can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard.

For site owners: Field monitor is its own section of My account with the widget's summary at the top (status, severity counts, Needs attention, Recently resolved, a traffic chart and plan-usage gauges), Diagnostics can be filtered to critical, warning or info, and Copy diagnostics copies a report-ready summary without email addresses, tokens or join codes.

For site owners: the home-screen widget's text is larger and grows with Android's font size instead of being cut off, the ✕ ! i counts open Diagnostics already filtered, and the widget settings screen shows a live preview, names each choice in words, applies a preset as soon as it is picked and shows a sample healthy preview in the Widgets list.
fixes: For site owners: the home-screen Field monitor widget now holds its own one-year owner session instead of borrowing the app's sign-in, so signing out of or back in to the app no longer leaves it on "Sign in". Disconnect widget revokes that session, and only the site owner can open or use the widget. Reconnect once after updating to move an existing widget to its own session.

Large campaigns save online again: a DM edit sends only the part of the campaign it changed, campaign artwork is stored beside the campaign online so it no longer counts toward the size limit, and edits to unrelated parts made on two devices no longer conflict.
Players who open an NPC from a link or refresh the NPC page can speak to that NPC again, as their own character.
When the DM awards encounter loot, the One purse coin option reads normally instead of squeezing into a one-letter column.
Treasure pool: an unclaimed item shows No claims yet, Claim all as Pass marks only the items you haven't answered, and Fairness explains that no loot has been handed out yet instead of rows of 0 cp.
The human check appears on the sign-in form after a recovery-key password reset, so signing in no longer fails until the page is reloaded.

summary: Split the party into groups, more NPC services from fences to stables, a fairness ledger, and an easier-to-find journey planner.
features: Split the party: the DM can split the party into up to six groups, each with a letter and colour, at different places, and merge them back when they meet again. Everyone stays in the party, so the shared purse, treasure pool, fairness totals and coin splits work as before.

Each group has its own map marker and Here list, and shops, services, nearby NPCs and property for sale follow where each character's group is. A journey moves one group, one approval can move every group the DM ticks, and a whole group can board a ship together.

Players see which group they're with and where the others are, unless the DM hides a group's place, and can ask the DM to move their group; the request waits in the Review Inbox. Update every phone in a split campaign: older apps ask to update before acting for a character who is with another group.

Fairness: Party → Fairness adds up the coins and items each character has received, campaign to date or for one session, with how far each is ahead of or behind the party average. Tap a character to see the receipts behind their total.
When handing out the treasure pool, the DM can choose Favour whoever is behind: Need still comes before Greed, and ties and round-robin go to whoever has received least.

Fences, banks, hirelings and tailors: a fence opens their shop's Sell tab while the black market is open, a bank opens a loan request with the bank named, an agent can propose hired hands for one of the party's properties, and tailors make clothes over approved downtime (bring your own cloth to pay less).

Sages identify an item your character carries. Nothing is charged while the DM considers it; the fee is charged once when the DM answers, and the answer arrives in your private conversation with the sage.
Trainers give paid lessons. Agree terms in conversation, then log each session in Downtime under Learn from a paid teacher; each session's fee is charged once when the DM approves it.
Couriers carry letters to NPCs your character has met, priced by distance. The letter travels as the DM approves downtime and arrives in your private conversation with that NPC.

Stables board your horses and mules by the night, with feed if you like, and coaches carry the party: booking a coach sends a journey request to the DM with the fare, charged once when the DM approves departure.
improvements: Plan journey is now a labelled button under Here on the map, and you can also start a journey from the Here sheet or from Travel at the top of the Downtime screen. On phones the map stays visible above the planner, journey progress shows a bar, Undo removes the last waypoint, and optional costs show their price before you turn them on.

Online campaigns: each account can host up to 2 online campaigns at a time, and Start a room and My account show how many you host. At the limit, close or delete one, or keep playing on your device. Joining campaigns as a player and playing on your device stay unlimited, and nothing you already host is closed.
New encounter awards record each item's value, so it counts in Fairness at the value the DM reviewed.

For site owners with the home-screen Field monitor: a redesigned widget with severity labels, how long each problem has lasted, problems resolved in the last 24 hours, and At a glance charts you can tap to expand. It can be resized down to 4×2, and the 4×1 companion has a new optional Status + charts preset.
fixes: For site owners: connecting the home-screen Field monitor no longer disconnects it again when the first reading is slow; it stays connected and retries.

summary: Party journeys across the map, NPC services at temples, workshops and inns, and community profiles for finding a group.
features: Party journeys: plan a route on the map, then Review journey turns it into a downtime preview with your pace, each day of travel and optional rations and mount upkeep. The DM chooses Approve & depart, the party marker follows the route as downtime is approved, and on arrival the DM confirms Move party here.

Players can send journey requests to the DM, who can approve them in one step from the Review Inbox. Players see the planned route where the map is visible to them, or a short text card when it is private.
Services in NPC conversations: asking an NPC about services lists every service they run and says plainly why one can't be used right now.
Temples: priests heal, lift curses and raise the dead for a price, with SRD prices or the DM's own. Raise Dead and Resurrection go to the DM first and are charged only if approved.
Workshops: order spell scrolls from scribes and potions from alchemists. You pay once when you order, the work moves forward with approved downtime, and you collect it at the workshop.
Inns: book rooms and meals for the party, paid once up front, and buy rumours that arrive in your private chat with the innkeeper.

Community profile in My account: choose a handle, whether you DM, play or both, your games, time zone, play times and an optional Discord username, and who can see it, for the Find a group directory on lootsplitter.com. Profiles stay hidden until you choose, and email addresses are never shown.
improvements: The Downtime screen shows blacksmith and workshop work together under Commissions, and Market's Service commission register tracks your orders while you travel.
Temples, workshops and inns appear on the map's Here sheet and on the shop's place card.
fixes: Treasure pool Activity lists claims and resolutions in the order they happened, even when two happen at the same moment.

summary: A new kobold app icon, even coin splits, and maps you can travel through: place cards, Show on map and a Here sheet.
features: New app icon and splash screen: the Lootsplitter kobold clutching a gold coin, including a themed icon for Android 13 and later.
Split coins evenly: split a party fund or an encounter's coins between party members in one step. Leftover copper goes to the party fund by default, and the DM can choose another rule.
Map pins open place cards: tap a pin to see the place, its status and what you can do there, and talk to an NPC straight from their pin.
Show on map: shops, NPCs, properties, listings and exchanges link to where they are on the map.
DMs can place a record on the map from its card, move or hide pins, and use a character's or NPC's portrait as their pin.
Here sheet on the map: one list of the shops, people and services available where the party is.
Maps: Consolidate fog shrinks heavily painted fog without changing what anyone sees, and grids can use the alternating 5/10/5 diagonal rule.
Journey planner: draw a route on a map to see each leg's distance, travel days and terrain, and send a drawn route to a ship voyage request.
Party treasure pool: the DM puts loot in the pool, players mark Need, Greed or Pass for their characters, and the DM hands items out fairly in one step from the Review Inbox.
improvements: Shared map images load from a cache instead of being re-sent with every change, so big maps update faster.
Players see a message while the DM's device is still updating the map, and screen readers announce token moves, pings and scene changes.
Website links in the app point to the new address, lootsplitter.com.
fixes: None in this release.

summary: Lootsplit is now Lootsplitter: same app, same data. The update installs over the existing app.
features: Lootsplit is now called Lootsplitter across the app, website, home-screen widgets and Help. Your campaigns, characters, settings, sign-in and placed widgets carry over unchanged.
improvements: Help explains the new name; backups and campaign copies saved under the old name still import.
Website pages, browser tab titles, notifications and the installed web app use the Lootsplitter name.
fixes: The installed web app (Add to home screen) is now named Lootsplitter instead of a generic placeholder name.

summary: Split view on tablets, NPC barter conversations, expandable widget rows with Cloudflare usage, and more reliable widgets and backups.
features: Split view on tablets in landscape: open two screens side by side in one window, for example your character sheet beside the map.

Barter with NPCs in conversation: make an offer, get a counter-offer, and a Persuasion roll against a difficulty set by how fair the deal is decides the answer. The DM chooses whether they decide each offer or the game rolls.
DM setting Party can see companion NPC funds (off by default) lets players in the party see the coins of visible NPCs travelling with them.
DMs can repair an estate property bought without its operating record with Set up operations, at no charge.
Owner Field monitor widget: tap a log row to expand it and read the full text, tap again to collapse, or press OPEN to go to the matching screen.
Owner Field monitor widget: Cloudflare plan usage rows (requests, CPU time and database reads and writes) for today, the last 7 days and the billing cycle that renews on the 11th.
improvements: When an action fails, the app now says so and keeps your input, instead of looking like it worked. Retrying never applies a payment, gift or purchase twice.
Offline (device) campaigns now handle buying, selling, gifts and listing purchases exactly like shared rooms.
Clearer widget status: a problem that has already stopped shows as attention rather than failure, and the multiplayer check is a real test round trip.
A healthy widget reading turns amber only after 35 minutes, matching the background refresh, and widget sync counts only phones seen in the last week.
Large campaigns with long session history keep saving, and restored campaigns keep their full history.
Smoother shared rooms: fewer unnecessary refreshes while nothing changes.
fixes: Privacy: players no longer receive NPC or exchange treasury balances, and only players whose character is in the party see other party members' balances.
The widget stays connected through a temporary storage error on the phone (it shows Widget storage busy and retries) and finishes refreshes within its time limit.
Android backups no longer carry your account sign-in to a new phone or reinstall; your campaigns and settings are still backed up.
Finance actions in offline campaigns with a blacksmith no longer fail.
Buying an imported estate listing keeps its property details, and storage accepts exact fits such as 0.1 lb items filling 0.3 lb.
Party chat keeps what you type right after opening a room, and messages send while your character is still loading.
Property import no longer reports unchanged data as changed, item weights no longer show long decimals, and device rolls are labeled DEVICE ROLL.

summary: Redesigned Android widgets, Agent activity on the 4×1 companion and a new app icon.
features: Agent activity preset for the 4×1 companion: the latest GitHub development activity (runs, pull requests, merges and deploys) with a status symbol and age, refreshed about every minute while a workflow runs and the screen is on.
New Lootsplit coin-and-quill app icon and splash screen, with a monochrome layer for themed icons.
improvements: Redesigned Field monitor widget: one status symbol and reason, four stat tiles, a task card with its timer, and a log that lists items needing attention first.
Redesigned 4×1 companion with the same status symbols, icon actions and larger touch targets.
Agent activity is the default for newly placed companions; existing companions keep their saved preset and every earlier preset remains available.
Your email is no longer shown on the home-screen widget; it stays in My account.
fixes: The companion no longer shows a stray “?” status.
Unavailable GitHub activity is labeled with its reason instead of appearing empty.

summary: Android companion widget discovery and installation recovery.
features: None in this release.
improvements: Add the 4×1 companion with its default Development preset and customize it from Settings after placement.
Add either widget before connecting owner access; private readings still require authorization.
Refresh widget list provides a safe recovery action and reports whether Android detects both types.
fixes: Reannounce both widget providers after an app update and on first launch, preserving placed widgets and saved settings.
Keep the compact companion identity row aligned within its bounds on high-density displays.
Validate both entries in Android’s actual widget picker and the signed APK upgrade/companion installation path before publication.

summary: Synchronized owner monitoring, daily reports and configurable Android companion.
features: Persistent backend monitoring every 30 minutes, daily calendar reports and a central registry that includes future logs.
Shared development tasks, persistent timing, component diagnostics and explicit coverage/stall warnings.
Independent 4×1 companion widgets with per-instance presets, summaries, toolbar actions and themes.
improvements: Shared website and Android account monitoring, bounded web scrolling and native main-widget collections.
Dated snapshots, source freshness, historical recovery, exports and performance-log cross-references.
Supported native elapsed timers and reduced-motion website warnings.
fixes: Retains direct home-screen refresh independently of My account and explains actual sign-in requirements.
Preserves confirmed component failures during disconnection and rejects out-of-order snapshots/task updates.

features: None in this release.
improvements: Last dated widget readings remain visible during refresh and temporary connection failures.
Repeated refresh taps share one bounded check, with clear retry feedback.
fixes: The home-screen Refresh button checks directly without requiring My account to be opened or the owner account to be reconnected.
A slow or failed request no longer leaves the widget indefinitely waiting for a background job.

summary: Private Android owner Field monitor and the current mobile Maps workspace.
features: Resizable green terminal home-screen Field monitor for the site owner, showing their authenticated account, service checks, account activity, app analytics and recent development/deployment activity.
Includes the current Maps workspace, connected scenes, encounter handoff, protected map media, fog and drawing tools.
improvements: Connect, add, refresh and disconnect the home-screen widget from My account; the in-app and website interfaces retain Lootsplit’s theme.
Dated readings, explicit unavailable sources and battery-aware background checks make monitoring status clear.
Packages the current campaign controls, role-specific Help and preserved account recovery flows.
fixes: Mobile Maps controls fit narrow portrait and landscape screens while preserving accessible tools and camera controls.
Widget sign-out, account changes and rejected owner access clear private readings; an older in-flight request cannot restore them.

summary: Current campaign tools, training bookkeeping and more efficient shared sync.
features: NPC training with hourly downtime budgets, DM reviews, category totals and manual milestone resets.
Current map grids/routes, property operations, commodity exchanges, bilateral barter, blacksmith commissions and local reference OCR are included in this Android update.
improvements: Authenticated unchanged-room reads avoid repeatedly transferring complete campaign snapshots; manual refresh and legacy clients retain full reads.
Atomic command batches share one private working copy while retaining every validation and retry receipt.
Character away actions accept elapsed campaign hours; calendar, usable downtime and training-day units are explicit.
fixes: Late training bookkeeping can be explicitly confirmed against historical location and levels without bypassing access or original hour budgets.
Training subject spacing/case variants share a counter while original descriptions and lifetime history remain intact.
Cloudflare CPU and private persistent-log settings are pinned in verified release artifacts; failure-email readiness is reported honestly.

summary: Keep rooms online for player viewing between sessions.
features: DMs can end a session while keeping the room online so players retain their assigned sheets and permitted campaign information.
After ending play, DMs can leave the room online and return through their account.
improvements: Player gameplay, chat, campaign-sheet changes, imports and rolls pause until the DM resumes play.
The existing End session option still closes the room and revokes player access; guest storage, privacy and current account-resume recovery are preserved.
fixes: None in this release.

summary: Safer account campaign reopening and recovery of unsynced device changes.
features: Device recovery copies can be exported when older queued changes belong to a different seat or conflict with the saved campaign.
improvements: Live changes and unfinished turn actions are labeled separately in sync recovery.
The startup campaign selector shows campaign IDs to distinguish separate saves with the same name.
fixes: Account campaign resume reconciles server acknowledgements before treating cached actions as unsynced, removing the false unfinished-turn blocker.
Genuine unsynced actions and server turn drafts remain reachable through Multiplayer recovery while preserving command and retry identifiers.
Older-seat device actions are preserved separately and are not replayed with another seat’s permissions.

summary: Larger DM shops, unified campaign control, and dedicated player finance and property services.
features: DMs can create suggested, chosen-count or all-matching shop assortments, including mixed markets, with independently selected stock quantities.
Existing shops support bulk catalog selection, fixed or unlimited quantities, stock summaries, search, filters and paginated shelves.
Player Home provides six fixed service buttons for Character Sheet, Bank, My Finances, Properties, Journal and Party chat.
Includes DM-reviewed character imports, campaign-day shop schedules and restocking, and property income and upkeep plans.
improvements: DM Desk and campaign overview share one Campaign control screen with five swipeable information panels, grouped tools and visible Multiplayer settings.
Dedicated Bank, finance, property, downtime and report screens separate player services from DM approvals and administration.
Bulk additions preserve existing custom prices and stock; pagination preserves complete saved inventories and PDF exports.
Brings the bundled Android client up to date with the verified website while retaining the package, permanent certificate, existing saves and supported play modes.
fixes: Removes small automatic assortment limits that excluded eligible catalog items from shops.
Saved DM shortcut destinations wait for account preferences instead of exposing incorrect defaults while loading.
The DM Review Inbox no longer includes a misplaced payment-request composer, and duplicate multiplayer entries are removed from the DM overview.

summary: Account-owned campaigns, safer shared sessions, refreshed themes and optional fantasy sounds.
features: Animated opening scene with a loot-hauling adventurer, coin-collecting rogue, and reduced-motion support.
Adventurer’s Ledger light theme and Ironbound Dragon dark theme, plus Pen & Paper and Virtual roll modes.
Optional CC0 coin, loot and page-turn sound effects, with device volume and preview controls; automatic sounds default off.
Account-owned DM campaigns with explicit End session, expiring invitations and guest play without persistent campaign storage.
Party Add loot supports Open5e search and custom items; scanned character/statblock imports offer local OCR and review.
improvements: Brings the bundled Android interface up to date with the verified website, retaining existing campaigns, exports and permanent signing identity.
DMs can resume saved campaigns across devices, reopen ended sessions, and control character editing and granular player permissions.
Clearer room selection, automatic membership linking and pending-upload feedback help prevent duplicate rooms and unsaved portraits.
Includes updated journal, encounter, loot, notification and owner testing controls.
fixes: Internal navigation no longer restarts the title screen when opening account, journal or ledger pages.
Shared player invitations point to the intended room and character and ask before switching an existing session.
Imported characters remain selected when older list requests finish, and filled PDF fields preserve supported values for review.
Character assignment, Live updates and inventory awards retain authorization and duplicate-award protections.

summary: Connected character sheets, reliable campaign switching, and safer inventory transfers.
features: The Android client now includes the current Dungeon Master control panel, player tools, settings panels, encounters, manual gameplay and loot review.
Party readouts and character sheets share character stats, funds and inventory, with permissions protecting changes.
improvements: Imported character levels and skill, save and initiative bonuses carry through to character displays and the dice tray.
Item transfers retain notes, weight, artwork, category and equipped state across local, shared and manual play.
The familiar mobile formatting and expanded desktop layout are preserved.
fixes: Older character editors no longer discard advanced sheet details or bypass Dungeon Master read-only protection.
Local dice rolls now use the saved character's bonuses.
Switching campaigns, reloading account characters and opening player links selects the intended character without stale permission errors.
Existing long inventory names, notes and IDs no longer prevent HP changes from saving.
Multiple queued offline gifts are preserved, and replaying a transfer report cannot award the same items twice.

summary: Safer Android exports, clearer shared-room switching, and verified release downloads.
features: Android exports offer Save file alongside Share, so you can choose a persistent location outside app storage.
New campaigns start with the Greyhaven default party; existing campaigns remain unchanged.
New ledger events record explicit transaction types and structured price history.
improvements: Joining an invitation while already connected offers an explicit choice and creates a backup before switching rooms.
Backup recovery guidance is clearer, including the limits of device-local backups and browser background notifications.
Release downloads include checksums, automated release checks and verification of the permanent signing certificate.
fixes: Cancelling a Save file export keeps the campaign and named device backup intact; successful saving is reported after the file has been written and closed.
